gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: The storm did considerable ___ to the harbour wall.
gaps.explanation: 'Do damage' — uncountable; 'damages' means money awarded in court.

gaps.sentence: We had lunch, and ___ we went for a walk.
gaps.explanation: 'Then' means next or after that; 'than' is used in comparisons.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the film, the hero rides off into the sunset.
gaps.hint: the final part of something (film, book, street)
gaps.explanation: 'At the end of something' refers to the final part; 'in the end' means finally, after a process.

gaps.sentence: We ___ money by cycling to work instead of driving.
gaps.hint: to keep money instead of spending it
gaps.explanation: 'Save money by doing something' means to avoid spending it; 'earn' means to receive money for work.

gaps.hint: the uncountable activity of travelling in general
gaps.explanation: 'Travel' is uncountable when it means travelling in general; the other options are countable nouns.
